label: Harm from one more tonne of CO₂e

rows.label: Heat deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂e (Rethink Priorities, GIVE model)

source.title: Clare & Vargas (2026), Cross-cause cost-effectiveness: climate change versus global health and development interventions, Rethink Priorities
source.page: Calculating the Mortality Cost of Carbon: Heat-Related Deaths, p. 16–17
source.quote: we estimate that the heat-related MCC is 4.31 × 10⁻⁵ (95% CI: 2.41 × 10⁻⁵ – 8.31 × 10⁻⁵)

rows.explainer: Deaths from higher temperatures, counted until 2300, caused by one extra tonne of CO₂ emitted in 2020: Rethink Priorities re-ran the GIVE model (Rennert et al. 2022, the model behind the US EPA's social cost of carbon) and counted the deaths themselves rather than their dollar value, so future deaths count in full, wherever they happen. The range is Rethink's 95% interval.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths that come with one more tonne of CO₂e from fossil fuels (Rethink Priorities)

source.title: Clare & Vargas (2026), Cross-cause cost-effectiveness: climate change versus global health and development interventions, Rethink Priorities
source.page: Calculating the Mortality Cost of Carbon: Air Pollution Deaths, p. 17; Appendix C
source.quote: we estimate that the air-pollution MCC is 1.46 × 10⁻⁴ (95% CI: 2.48 × 10⁻⁵ – 4.28 × 10⁻⁴)

rows.explainer: Burning fossil fuels also releases fine particles, which kill far more people than the extra heat does. Rethink Priorities divides each paper's yearly deaths from fossil-fuel fine particles by that year's global emissions (Vohra et al. 2021: 2.93 per 10,000 tonnes; Lelieveld et al. 2023: 1.47; McDuffie et al. 2021: 0.30) and combines them with weights of 20%, 60% and 20%. It is an average: a tonne from coal carries more particles than a tonne from gas, and a tonne kept in a forest carries none.

rows.label: Deaths from heat and air pollution caused by one more tonne of CO₂e (Rethink Priorities)

source.title: Clare & Vargas (2026), Cross-cause cost-effectiveness: climate change versus global health and development interventions, Rethink Priorities
source.page: Appendix E (threshold BOTEC); Model 1 results, p. 18
source.quote: the median MCC estimate from our Model 1 Heat + Air Pollution (1.90E-04)

rows.explainer:
The default for the shared assumption "Deaths caused by one more tonne of CO₂": Rethink Priorities' median for heat and air-pollution deaths together, 1.9 per 10,000 tonnes. It matches Rethink's median cost per life saved of $10,517 at their median abatement cost of $2 a tonne (2 ÷ 10,517 = 1.9 per 10,000).

The low end, 0.43 per 10,000, is Rethink's heat-only scenario (no air-pollution deaths). The high end, 5.1 per 10,000, is the tops of Rethink's two 95% intervals added (heat 0.83, air pollution 4.28); it is also about what Rethink's whole-damages estimate, which adds crops, energy and sea-level rise (CG$1,600 a tonne at $100,000 per healthy year, 0.016 healthy years), comes to in lives at 32 healthy years each (5.0 per 10,000).

rows.label: Social cost of carbon (Rennert et al. 2022, GIVE model, 2020 dollars)

source.title: Rennert et al. (2022), Comprehensive evidence implies a higher social cost of CO₂, Nature 610, 687–692
source.quote: Our preferred mean SC-CO2 estimate is $185 per tonne of CO2 ($44-$413 per tCO2: 5%-95% range, 2020 US dollars) at a near-term risk-free discount rate of 2%

rows.explainer: A cross-check, not read by any model. The damage, in dollars, of one more tonne of CO₂: $90 of the $185 is heat deaths, valued at a rich-country price of a life that falls with income and is discounted at 2% a year. Rethink Priorities' re-run of the same model is where the heat-death count (0.43 per 10,000 tonnes) comes from, so the two agree on the deaths and differ only in how they are valued.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e cut to save one life (Giving What We Can, 2016)

source.title: Wilkinson (2016), Modelling climate change cost-effectiveness, Giving What We Can
source.quote: to save one life, we would have to reduce emissions by 258,200t (with lower bound of 179,400t)

rows.explainer: A cross-check, not read by any model: Giving What We Can's older and cruder estimate, 0.04 deaths per 10,000 tonnes (an older estimate in the same report, which it doesn't endorse, was 5,000 tonnes per healthy year). It counts far fewer deaths than Rethink Priorities because it leaves out air pollution and uses older damage estimates; it sits about 11 times below Rethink's heat-only figure, the low end of our range.
